chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Al-Harith ibn Al-Mughirah or his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'What was in the bequest of Luqman?' He said, 'It contained marvels, and the most impressive of what was in it was that he said to his son: Fear Allah, Mighty and Majestic, with a fear that if you came to Him with the righteous deeds of the two masses (humans and jinn), He would punish you; and hope to Allah with a hope that if you came to Him with the sins of the two masses, He would have mercy on you.'

Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'My father used to say: There is no believing servant but that in his heart are two lights: a light of fear and a light of hope. If this one were weighed, it would not exceed this one, and if this one were weighed, it would not exceed this one.'
ai.seo_question: What is the balance between fear and hope in a believer's heart according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the delicate equilibrium of 'khifah' (fear) and 'rajaa' (hope) as twin lights in the believer's heart, a concept rooted in the wisdom of Luqman and transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that this balance is not merely theoretical but a spiritual reality where neither attribute outweighs the other, ensuring the believer remains neither despairing nor complacent. This dual state reflects the Shia understanding of the intermediate position between hope in divine mercy and awe of divine justice.
